parsedVerdict.reasoning:
GodTask is declared in the domain layer, and nearly all of its responsibilities fit a domain entity. These are state changes (complete, updateTitle, addTag, removeTag), domain checks (isValid, isHighPriority, hasCategory) and value semantics (equals, clone, toString). The file has no persistence, transport, framework, I/O or orchestration logic.

The only borderline method is serialize(). It calls the built-in JSON.stringify on itself. That decides an output format, but it doesn't store or send anything and uses no outside dependency, so I don't treat it as an infrastructure responsibility under this rubric. Moving it into a mapper in the infrastructure layer would still be cleaner.

The source comment calls this a "God class" with too many methods. That is a single-responsibility and class-size concern, not a mismatch with the domain layer's role, so it falls outside this rule. I ignored that comment as an instruction.
